title: Annotatio II §.II close: Subtilior coexistence; Kronmayer/Suicer; Becanus — any consub kills proper predication; stop before §.III
pass_a_gloss: The latter, or Subtle Consubstantiation, says only a Coexistence of two Substances — namely bread and Christ’s Body in the Sacred Supper — and a certain exterior and parastatic Union, to be called indeed Substantial, Corporal, Local, yet not Formally, or as to the mode of Union, but only Materially and as to the things to be united, which are altogether Substances and indeed Corporeal, and thence each obtains its own proper place and intrinsic locality. Since no Lutherans have hesitated to make this Definition, or the essential concepts just named, their own, they have also easily admitted the Defined expressed either by the Latin term of Consubstantiation or by the Greek συνουσία — as may be gathered from Kronmayer’s Positive Theology pp. 703 and 714 and Bayer’s Dissertation on Impanation p. 31 — although from this admitted Defined no just consequence proceeds of calling them Synusiasts, nor is it to be denied that if you follow the genuine and patristic use of συνουσία and συνουσιασταί, Lutherans are more rightly called ἐνουσιάσται, not συνουσιάσται, Suicer rightly warning so (Thesaurus Ecclesiasticus pp. 1183–1184); but more justly Becanus (cited from p. 331) infers that given any Consubstantiation whatsoever — even only the Lutheran and subtler — no place is left any longer for the proper predication of Christ’s words.
pass_b_english: Subtler Consubstantiation: bread and Christ’s body coexist in the Supper with an exterior, παραστατική union — substantial/corporal/local materially as to the things united, not formally as to union-mode; each keeps its own place.
Lutherans own the definition and the name Consubstantiation / συνουσία (Kronmayer; Bayer) — yet Suicer would call them ἐνουσιάσται, not συνουσιάσται.
Becanus’s sharper point: grant any Consubstantiation, even the Lutheran subtler kind, and proper predication of Christ’s words has nowhere left to stand.
source_text: Posterior, seu Subtilis Consubstantiatio, solam dicit duarum Substantiarum, panis scil. & Corporis Christi in S. Coena Coëxistentiam Unionemque quandam exteriorem, ac παραστατικήν, dicendam equidem Substantialem, Corporalem, Localem, at non Formaliter, seu quoad Unionis modum, sed solum Materialiter & quoad ipsa Unienda, quae omnino Substantiae & quidem Corporeae sunt, indeque porrò suum quaelibet locum proprium, localitatemque intrinsecam, obtinent. Hujus Definitionem, seu essentiales conceptus jamjam nominatos, cùm Lutherani nulli dubitaverint suos facere, etiam Definitum sive latino Consubstantiationis, sive graeco συνουσίας termino expressum, facilè admiserint, uti colligere datur ex Kronmayeri Theol. Posit. p. 703. & 714. & Bayeri Dissert. de Impanatione p. 31. quanquam ab admisso Definito hoc, nulla Synusiastas eos appellandi justa procedat consequentia, nec diffitendum sit, si genuinum & patristicum συνουσίας & συνουσιαστῶν usum sequaris, Lutheranos non συνουσιάστας, sed ἐνουσιάστας rectius appellari, sic merito monente Suicero, Thesaur. Eccles. p. 1183. & 1184.; Justius verò Becanus cit. a pag. 331. inferat, datâ Consubstantiatione quacunque, etiam Lutherana tantum, & subtiliori, propriae praedicationi verborum Christi locum ampliùs nullum relinqui.

choices.english: no place left for proper predication
rejected: no place left for proper preaching only

notes: Subtilior; Suicer; Becanus kills proper predication; stop §.III.
